catalog_quote: 本稿では、名詞および動詞の声調について、引用形で観察される声調のパターンを整理する。句や文での声調については未調査である。... ベンデ語の声調は、決して例は多くないが、語彙的および文法的弁別機能を持つ。音節ごとに高声調 H(igh)、低声調 L(ow)、上昇声調 R(ising)、下降声調 F(alling) の 4 種類の実現声調があるが、本稿では名詞の引用形、動詞の動名詞形を基に、いくつかの環境を設定してどのようなパターンあるか観察する。その結果、ベンデ語の声調は、音節数が増えてもパターンが限定的であり、基本的には 3 パターンである。すなわち、(a) 語幹がすべて H、(b) 接頭辞は H で語幹が L あるいは R ではじまるもの、(c) は接頭辞が L で語幹の次末音節に H ないし H を含む R や F が現れるものである。 [Abe 2021: 249] — [thesis p. 57] ベンデ語も大多数の Bantu 諸語と同様, 意味の区別に弁別的な声調を持つ. [p. 59] 語幹ないし語根の声調型には 3 種類あり, それぞれ H(igh) 型, L(ow) 型, 0 型と呼ぶことにする. H 型は語幹ないし語根が H で始まるもの, L 型は語幹ないし語根が L で始まるもの, 0 型は後ろから 2 番目の音節が H となり最終音節は再び L となるものである. 借用語の多くが 0 型で実現される.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: ベンデ語の声調は、決して例は多くないが、語彙的および文法的弁別機能を持つ。音節ごとに高声調 H(igh)、低声調 L(ow)、上昇声調 R(ising)、下降声調 F(alling) の 4 種類の実現声調があるが、本稿では名詞の引用形、動詞の動名詞形を基に、いくつかの環境を設定してどのようなパターンあるか観察する。その結果、ベンデ語の声調は、音節数が増えてもパターンが限定的であり、基本的には 3 パターンである。すなわち、(a) 語幹がすべて H、(b) 接頭辞は H で語幹が L あるいは R ではじまるもの、(c) は接頭辞が L で語幹の次末音節に H ないし H を含む R や F が現れるものである。
new_statements.translation: Bende tone has lexical and grammatical distinctive function, though the examples are by no means numerous. Each syllable carries one of four surface tones, High, Low, Rising, Falling; here, on the basis of noun citation forms and verb gerund (infinitive) forms, several environments are set up to observe what patterns exist. The result is that Bende tone patterns remain limited even as the number of syllables grows: there are basically three patterns, namely (a) stem all H, (b) prefix H with the stem beginning in L or R, and (c) prefix L with H (or an R or F containing H) appearing on the penultimate syllable of the stem.
new_statements.citation: 阿部優子 [Abe, Yuko]. 2021. ベンデ語の声調 [Tone in Bende]. In 梶茂樹 (ed.), アフリカ諸語の声調・アクセント = Tone and Accent in African Languages, pp.249-278. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. (CC BY 4.0; JaLC DOI 10.15026/99923). Corroborated by Abe 2006 PhD thesis (TUFS) ch.3 sec.1, pp.57-59 and ch.2 sec.1.4, p.30.
new_statements.locator: sec.1, p.249 (restated sec.4, p.261 and sec.5, p.272); thesis quotes at pp.57, 59 and p.30
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Copies checked (1) Abe 2021, ベンデ語の声調, ILCAA, CC BY 4.0, text): the quoted passage is on p.249, sec.1, verbatim (whitespace-insensitive string match = True against extracted text output); the three-pattern statement is restated at sec.4 (p.261) and sec.5 (p.272) as the compiler says. Whole-chapter keyword scan: アクセント occurs once, only in the footnote naming the ILCAA project title; 強勢/ストレス/stress/accent/卓立/プロミネンス = 0 hits. Conclusion (pp.276-277) read: open problems are the 2-syllable H window after L and affix tone; phrase/sentence tone explicitly uninvestigated. No stress/accent analysis anywhere. (2) Abe 2006 TUFS PhD thesis, image-only scans rendered and read: p.57 'ベンデ語も大多数の Bantu 諸語と同様…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bende is described purely as a (restricted) tone language: every noun/verb stem belongs to one of three lexical tonal classes (thesis: H-type, L-type, 0-type); the 0-type/pattern (c), which absorbs most Swahili loans and prefixless words, places a single H on the word's penultimate syllable with a final L (2σ HL/RL, 3σ LHL, 4σ LLHL), while H-type words are all-H and L-type words have prefix H then L followed by H held for two syllables. Neither source posits word stress or accent; the thesis (p.30) attributes all vowel length to lexical length or vowel concatenation, i.e. no penultimate lengthening, and vowel length is contrastive.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned (no stress analysis at all).
new_statements.exceptions: R and F occur only on long vowels or next to CG/NC (predictable); syllabic-less nasal prefixes cannot bear H, whose floating H docks onto a preceding copula ni (nǐ ɱfukú); after an L (copula ni, or L-initial stems) an H stretch is limited to two syllables; two verb conjugations (βá-ná-..-e, βa-na-..-a) neutralise all three tonal classes to L; monosyllabic 0-type kufwǎ 'die' puts the R/H on the prefix-adjacent syllable when extended (kufwǐla). Phrase- and sentence-level tone explicitly uninvestigated.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms of nouns and ku- infinitives, plus copula (ni +) and preposition (ná +) frames and one finite tense; word-level lexical tone, not phrasal prominence. The penultimate-H of the 0-type is a lexical tone class default, not described as stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Both primary sources describe Bende as spoken around Katuma village, Mpanda District (Katavi/Rukwa), west Tanzania; Abe treats Bende (F12, bend1258) and Tongwe (F11, Glottolog tong1321) as two dialects of one language, but her data are Bende proper.

tone.quote: The database ICULD-0043 contains recordings of Bende Words produced by a male speaker in Tanzania in 2001. Bende (F12) is a Bantu language spoken in the Katavi region in Western Tanzania by an estimated 41,490 speakers. It is a language isolate and has varieties with or without pitch accent. This database has 9011 tokens compiled from two repetitions of about 4500 items.
